paper_title: Progressive evolutions of non-fused ring electron acceptors toward efficient organic solar cells with improved photocurrent and reduced energy loss

qa_pairs.question: What is the peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) of the organic solar cell based on the J52:O-PC-EH blend, and what is its certified value?
qa_pairs.answer: The organic solar cell based on the J52:O-PC-EH blend achieved a peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 14.43%, with a certified value of 14.1%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Progressive evolutions of non-fused ring electron acceptors toward efficient organic solar cells with improved photocurrent and reduced energy loss

qa_pairs.question: Describe the molecular evolution process from DF-PCIC to the O-PC-X series of non-fused ring electron acceptors (NFREAs).
qa_pairs.answer: The molecular evolution begins with the terminal fluorination of DF-PCIC to form HF-PCIC. Subsequently, the fluorine atoms on the core of HF-PCIC are replaced with alkoxy groups—either linear (O-PC-OC) or branched (O-PC-EH)—to tune the optoelectronic properties.
qa_pairs.source_title: Progressive evolutions of non-fused ring electron acceptors toward efficient organic solar cells with improved photocurrent and reduced energy loss

qa_pairs.question: How do intramolecular noncovalent interactions affect the molecular geometry of the NFREAs such as O-PC-EH and HF-PCIC?
qa_pairs.answer: Intramolecular F...H and O...S noncovalent interactions help lock the molecular geometry into a planar configuration. This planarity is confirmed by DFT calculations, which show relatively small dihedral angles for these molecules.
qa_pairs.source_title: Progressive evolutions of non-fused ring electron acceptors toward efficient organic solar cells with improved photocurrent and reduced energy loss

qa_pairs.question: What effect does the introduction of electron-donating alkoxy groups onto the core of NFREAs have on their energy levels and device energy loss?
qa_pairs.answer: The introduction of electron-donating alkoxy groups effectively up-shifts the HOMO levels of the NFREAs. This narrows the energetic offset between the donor and acceptor, which in turn reduces the overall energy loss in the organic solar cell.
qa_pairs.source_title: Progressive evolutions of non-fused ring electron acceptors toward efficient organic solar cells with improved photocurrent and reduced energy loss

qa_pairs.question: What are the non-radiative voltage loss and energetic offset values for the J52:O-PC-EH-based device?
qa_pairs.answer: The J52:O-PC-EH-based device exhibits a low non-radiative voltage loss (ΔVnon-rad) of 0.301 V and a small energetic offset (ΔECT) of 0.090 eV.
qa_pairs.source_title: Progressive evolutions of non-fused ring electron acceptors toward efficient organic solar cells with improved photocurrent and reduced energy loss

qa_pairs.question: How do the photovoltaic parameters (Voc, Jsc, and FF) of the optimal J52:O-PC-EH device compare to its performance metrics?
qa_pairs.answer: The optimal J52:O-PC-EH device achieves a PCE of 14.43% through an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.819 V, a short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 24.44 mA cm-2, and a fill factor (FF) of 72.2%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Progressive evolutions of non-fused ring electron acceptors toward efficient organic solar cells with improved photocurrent and reduced energy loss

qa_pairs.question: According to GIWAXS characterization, how does the crystal coherence length (CCL) of O-PC-EH compare to DF-PCIC and HF-PCIC in the in-plane direction?
qa_pairs.answer: O-PC-EH exhibits a significantly higher crystal coherence length (CCL) of 250.06 Å in the in-plane direction, whereas the CCLs for DF-PCIC and HF-PCIC are much smaller, ranging between 20 and 40 Å.
qa_pairs.source_title: Progressive evolutions of non-fused ring electron acceptors toward efficient organic solar cells with improved photocurrent and reduced energy loss

qa_pairs.question: What are the exciton-dissociation and charge-collection efficiencies for the J52:O-PC-EH-based organic solar cell?
qa_pairs.answer: The J52:O-PC-EH-based device demonstrates an exciton-dissociation efficiency (Pdiss) of 96.03% and a charge-collection efficiency (Pcoll) of 81.86%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Progressive evolutions of non-fused ring electron acceptors toward efficient organic solar cells with improved photocurrent and reduced energy loss
